title: ScalaGBM: Memory Efficient GBDT Training for High-Dimensional Data on GPU

problem.claim: Histogram-based GBDT training on millions of features requires substantial memory for training data and histograms, creating challenges on GPUs with limited memory.

gap.claim: Existing GBDT frameworks can run out of memory when training high-dimensional datasets on a single GPU.

contributions.claim: ScalaGBM is a GPU-based GBDT framework designed to accelerate high-dimensional data training with lower memory usage.
ScalaGBM uses a CSR-like data format and CSR-based histogram construction to reduce training-data memory occupation.
ScalaGBM reorganizes the training workflow with a double-buffer structure to reduce overall histogram memory consumption.

author_reported_evidence.claim: ScalaGBM reportedly handles real-world datasets with over 100 million instances and 50 million features on a single commercial GPU, while existing GBDT frameworks run out of memory.
ScalaGBM reportedly achieves a maximum 39× speedup over state-of-the-art GBDT counterparts without sacrificing training quality.

narrative_sequence.summary: GBDTs are widely used in recommendation systems and database queries, and GPUs are used to accelerate histogram-based training.
High-dimensional training data and histograms can exceed the memory capacity of limited-memory GPUs.
ScalaGBM reduces memory through CSR-like data and histogram construction, then uses double buffering for histogram memory.
The framework accelerates training with multidimensional parallel histogram construction and global optimal split-point reduction.
The authors report successful single-GPU handling of very large datasets and up to 39× speedup without sacrificing training quality.

source_observation.claim: Reducing the memory footprint of both training data and histograms is central to handling high-dimensional GBDT workloads on limited-memory GPUs.

interpretation.claim: Memory optimization may require coordinated changes to data representation and intermediate-workspace organization.

application.claim: For GPU training systems constrained by data and histogram memory, consider sparse or compact representations together with bounded buffering.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether these techniques generalize beyond the reported GBDT workloads and datasets.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, hardware configuration, or baseline framework versions used in the experiments.
The abstract does not define the training-quality metric or quantify the memory reductions.
The abstract does not provide implementation details for the parallel histogram construction or split-point reduction.
